skill.name: insforge-integrations
skill.description: Guide InsForge projects through third-party authentication, JWT-based row-level security, and OKX x402 payment integration.
skill.summary: Build InsForge authentication and x402 payment integrations with provider-specific setup, code, database, and verification guidance.
skill.author: insforge

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives caused by documentation, placeholders, structured encoding, and intended provider calls. Semantic review found critical payment-signing weaknesses, a production payment bypass risk, and public exposure of linked payment metadata.

remediation.issue: Mock mode requests a real EIP-3009 transfer authorization.
remediation.suggestion: Use a test chain or a non-transferable mock signature. Never request a production-token authorization while mock mode is active.

remediation.issue: The client signs unvalidated payment challenge fields.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist the network, asset, recipient, domain, maximum amount, and timeout before showing confirmation or calling signTypedData.

remediation.issue: The mock facilitator can remain enabled in production.
remediation.suggestion: Fail startup when mock mode is enabled under production. Require a development-only build setting in addition to the environment flag.

remediation.issue: Payment rows and realtime events expose linked usage metadata publicly.
remediation.suggestion: Require authorization, minimize returned fields, and restrict RLS policies to owners or an explicitly approved public aggregate.

semantic_findings.title: Mock Mode Still Requests a Real Transfer Authorization
semantic_findings.description: The guide states that mock mode still asks the wallet for a real EIP-3009 signature. A reusable authorization may expose test users to unintended settlement.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide explicitly says mock mode preserves real wallet signing, and the sample calls signTypedData for TransferWithAuthorization.

semantic_findings.title: Payment Challenge Is Signed Without Client Validation
semantic_findings.description: The client signs the first challenge entry without enforcing expected network, token, recipient, amount, domain, or timeout limits. A compromised endpoint could request an unintended authorization.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The sample copies every security-sensitive field from the decoded challenge into signTypedData and performs only an empty-array check.

semantic_findings.title: Mock Configuration Can Bypass Paid Endpoint Enforcement
semantic_findings.description: A single environment flag makes verification and settlement succeed without cryptographic checks. If enabled outside local development, arbitrary callers can receive paid content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The MOCK branches return successful verification and settlement results, with no runtime guard that restricts them to development.

semantic_findings.title: Payment Metadata Is Publicly Queryable
semantic_findings.description: The sample grants public reads and returns recent payment rows without authentication. This exposes wallet addresses, endpoints, amounts, and transaction hashes as linked usage records.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The SQL policy permits all SELECT operations, and the unauthenticated GET handler returns complete recent rows through a service client.

content.user_title: Build InsForge Auth and x402 Integrations
content.value_statement: Connecting external identity and payment providers to InsForge requires careful token, database, and protocol setup. This skill provides provider-specific implementation and verification guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains JWT integration patterns for Clerk, Auth0, WorkOS, Kinde, Stytch, and Better Auth.
Provides InsForge client examples that attach provider-backed access tokens.
Defines database helpers and row-level security policies for string user identifiers.
Shows Better Auth schema isolation, bridge routes, token refresh, and framework variants.
Documents an OKX x402 payment flow with verification, settlement, storage, and realtime updates.
Includes setup checks, environment variable lists, and provider-specific troubleshooting guidance.
limitations: The guides require external provider accounts, credentials, and dashboard configuration.
Examples target specific frameworks and may require adaptation for other application stacks.
The x402 guide involves wallet signatures and real digital-asset transfers.
Users must independently review provider versions, production security, and legal requirements.

use_cases.title: Add SaaS Authentication
use_cases.description: Connect an existing identity provider to InsForge and enforce per-user database access.

use_cases.title: Deploy Self-Hosted Authentication
use_cases.description: Run Better Auth against InsForge Postgres with isolated tables and a JWT bridge.

use_cases.title: Prototype Paid API Access
use_cases.description: Build an x402 endpoint that verifies payment, settles through OKX, and records results.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Auth Provider
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the supported authentication providers for my InsForge application and recommend one based on these requirements: [requirements].

prompt_templates.title: Implement Provider Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate [provider] with this InsForge project. Add token handling, required environment variables, and protected database access.

prompt_templates.title: Add Row-Level Security
prompt_templates.prompt: Create InsForge SQL for a [table] table using string user IDs, requesting_user_id(), and owner-only row-level security policies.

prompt_templates.title: Harden an x402 Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this OKX x402 implementation. Validate challenge fields, isolate mock mode, protect payment metadata, and produce a production checklist.

output_examples.input: Connect Clerk to an InsForge notes application with owner-only access.
output: A Clerk JWT template configuration using the InsForge signing secret.
A client token-refresh flow that updates InsForge authentication state.
A notes table design with string user IDs and owner-only policies.

output_examples.input: Plan a Better Auth integration for a Vite application and InsForge Postgres.
output: A dedicated Better Auth schema and migration sequence.
A server bridge that validates sessions and issues short-lived InsForge tokens.
A same-origin proxy plan with cookie and origin requirements.

output_examples.input: Design a secure OKX x402 endpoint for a paid report.
output: A payment challenge flow with explicit network, asset, amount, and recipient checks.
A facilitator verification and settlement sequence with failure handling.
A private payment ledger and production readiness checklist.

best_practices: Keep signing secrets, database credentials, and service keys on trusted server processes.
Validate token claims and payment challenge fields before granting access or requesting signatures.
Test row-level security, token refresh, mock isolation, settlement errors, and retry behavior before production.
anti_patterns: Do not expose service keys or provider secrets through browser-prefixed environment variables.
Do not use UUID-only identity helpers when the external provider issues string user identifiers.
Do not enable payment mock mode or accept unvalidated wallet challenges in production.

faq.question: Which authentication providers are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers Clerk, Auth0, WorkOS, Kinde, Stytch, and Better Auth.

faq.question: Does the skill configure provider dashboards automatically?
faq.answer: No. Provider applications, keys, callbacks, and dashboard settings require manual configuration.

faq.question: Why are InsForge user ID columns stored as text?
faq.answer: The supported external providers issue string identifiers that are not compatible with UUID-only columns.

faq.question: Can I use these examples outside Next.js?
faq.answer: Some patterns are framework-independent, and Better Auth includes Vite guidance. Other frameworks require adapted routing, sessions, and environment handling.

faq.question: Does the OKX x402 flow move real funds?
faq.answer: Yes. Production settlement uses wallet-signed USDG authorizations on X Layer and can transfer digital assets.

faq.question: Is the provided payment mock mode production-ready?
faq.answer: No. It bypasses verification and settlement, and the sample still requests a real wallet authorization.
